relevance_note: The paper describes one identifiable patient with Tangier disease: 'A case that we observed recently is a male of forty seven years old whose HDL cholesterol level was 6 mg/dl' (Fig.2, 'a case with Tangier disease'); no ABCA1 variant is reported.
method_note: Written by hand with a small Python script assembling the JSON; no table transcribed by script. The family lipid table has no caption in the Markdown; the text cites '(Table I)' for the Tangier case and the row '→II-1 Proband' matches the text (HDL-C 6, AI 3.9), so it is taken as Table I. Its rows (Mother, Sister, Brother, Wife, Daughter) are recorded as relatives of the proband with their own pedigree labels; the sister's label is printed 'I1-2' (probably a conversion error for II-2) and kept verbatim. Relatives' lipid values are given without interpretation, so no features are recorded for them. Proband's TG 232 mg/dl (controls 86±29) is not called abnormal in the text, so hypertriglyceridemia is left not reported. Low apoA-I is marked observed from the value 3.9 mg/dl together with 'Total cholesterol level is also markedly low'. No variant rows: the paper (1991) reports no ABCA1 variant and states 'neither have gene abnormalities of apoAI been demonstrated'. The four CETP-deficiency cases (Table II), the 5 CETP-deficient homozygotes and the two hepatic-lipase patients are out of scope; no single total cohort size is stated. How the Tangier diagnosis was made is not stated. No contradictions found.
